rulings.reasoning:
The exact delta V4 -> V5 of the span is confined to AR4-17, AR4-19, AR4-22 and V24R3-02, plus the three edges and editorial removals of finding labels. Every pointer in the agreed text resolves in the registered versions. The graph re-runs ALL_PASS byte-identically, and all prior findings on these sections are FIXED.

The agreement also does not depend on the outcome of the V2.5 verification: a V2.5 byte change would alter only section 4, and the section 1 procedure is generic ('V2.1, then each errata document in version order'). The section 218 order (V2.5 verification first) can still be kept.

rulings.item: AQ-V5-01, tuple facet only (EVM_FROZEN learned on PRODUCT_BUILD and consumed by CHARACTERIZATION_BUILD governing runs)
rulings.recommendation:
DEFER the main question to the BA-04/BA-06/BA-07 dimensions. Constraints from this dimension:
(1) V2.5 decides nothing about cross-build EVM use; each profile carries its own CATALOG_FOLDER (AR4-06 (2)).
(2) V2.1 27.5 says that any change to the tuple requires a new model version and revalidation. An answer given as a recorded reading, like AR4-06 (4), needs no contract text. An answer that adds a tuple field or amends 27.5 is a V2.6 micro-errata (the AR3-13 precedent) and must precede the BA-01 candidate.
(3) Whichever direction the build-equivalence record covers, it must compare the CATALOG_FOLDER file-hash sets of both profiles (BA11V5-05); otherwise the equivalence does not cover a BUILD_BOUND product-path input.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 2.1 and 2.2 make every BUILD_BOUND field part of the tuple, and a mismatch is INVALID. V2.5 adds CATALOG_FOLDER to that set. AR4-06 (1) and (2) record one profile per BUILD_UNDER_TEST with its own values, and AR4-06 (4) rules only the characterization-to-product direction.

That sentence lies outside sections 1..2.1, so the rule-5 agreement is unaffected, and BA-11 is sealed last, so there is no cascade.

findings.failure_scenario: NC-E12C on its detection branch: the witness records the Wr-A write at X6 delivered in W-scan. E12C FAILs and the outcome is O7, as declared. A2 is exercised with an expected PASS. The A-2 measurement of V2.1 14.7 counts that WRITE_CLASS event after V0, so the observation is A-2 FAIL, or UNKNOWN because no rule defines it. That differs from the declared PASS. Under V2.1 1.3 the designed detection of NC-E12C does not PASS, and under BA-02b rule 2 the EA2 group receives a FAIL or UNKNOWN. A-2 FAIL means CHARACTERIZED_DIFFERENT, so EA2 goes AMENDMENT_PENDING, caused by the harness's own injected write. NC-E12A's non-delivery branch has the same exposure when the XData notification is deferred past V0, although its declared W-scan is 'EMPTY'.

rulings.item: AQ-V5-01: whether the recorded build equivalence of AR4-06 (4) also covers EVM_FROZEN, learned and validated on the PRODUCT_BUILD and consumed by 111 governing CHARACTERIZATION_BUILD runs
rulings.recommendation:
RULE: YES. The recorded equivalence of AR4-06 (4) is the basis for this reverse direction too, and it is required, with these conditions.
(1) Add BUILD_EQUIVALENCE_RECORD to the RUN_PREREQUISITES of the 111 governing CHARACTERIZATION_BUILD scenarios that consume EVM_FROZEN. Each run cites the record hash in RUN_START (RUN_PREREQUISITE_RULE). Recompute their SEALED_AT and the counts of md sections 1.1, 2.1, 4 and 5.
(2) BA-07 V5 extends U5 and the 5.3 'Reverse direction' paragraph to a CHARACTERIZATION_BUILD run that consumes EVM_FROZEN: the record's REVIEW_RECORD_ADDED entry is covered by the run-start anchor, and the control plane checks this at run start.
(3) The method of the record must establish that the assemblies present only in the characterization build are event-neutral in the governed window unless a scenario names them. These are the switches, the injection points, the I-14 writers, the delivery-witness subscription, DRY_RUN_BRANCH_SWITCH and the declared canaries. This is the property V2.1 27.5 turns on.
(4) Without a cited record, EVM_FROZEN does not apply: the run is not started, or E12A and E12C cannot be PASS (fail-closed).
(5) EA2-DEFERRED-EVENTS, a clean characterization-build run whose phase A must equal f(plan), is the in-catalog safeguard, as E4-VAL-R1 is for the forward direction. A phase-A or phase-C difference seen only on the characterization build is recorded first as a finding against the equivalence. Adding the record to EA2's RUN_PREREQUISITES also anchors, per run, its AR4-06 (6) contribution to PARAM-03.
(6) Learning and validation stay on the PRODUCT_BUILD (AR4-01). There is no characterization-build model version.
rulings.reasoning:
- V2.1 27.5 lists the tuple among the changes that require 'a new model version, review and revalidation'.
- AR4-06 (1) gives each build its own admissible profile, and every run is compared with the profile of its own build (V2.1 2, 2.2). The EVM, however, was learned and validated only under the PRODUCT_BUILD profile. AR4-01 moved EV-L-* there precisely so that learning and validation share a build under 27.5 (CQ-08 'sin objeto').
- The only contract-grounded bridge between two profiles is the verified and recorded equivalence of AR4-06 (4): product assemblies byte-identical, with the switches in separate harness assemblies, or a reviewed diff. That content is symmetric, so it supports both directions.
- V2.1 3.2 (fail-closed) and V2.2 PA-2 (only a FROZEN model is used by governing validation) forbid relying on an equivalence that is not recorded.
- A NO would require a separate EVM version learned and validated on the characterization build (V2.1 27.2; PA-2). Until then NC-E12A, NC-E12C, the 18 E12C WR cells and NC-S5-O6 would have no usable model, and E12A and E12C would become NEGATIVE_CONTROL_MISSING in BA-02b.
- Applying the product model on the characterization build fails closed in effect: an extra or missing event aborts or FAILs. The residual risk is a false FAIL charged to E12-V, which conditions (3) and (5) address.

rulings.recommendation:
RULE: YES, by content and not by id prefix. AR4-06 (3) applies to every qualification control that V2.1 4.3.1, as amended by V2.2 PA-12, adds to the qualification of section 4.3.
- Add PR-CLOSURE-COMPLETENESS-CB (FX-IMP, K-8; PR-REC stays contract-assigned, evidence only).
- Add WU-BOUNDARY-CB (governing, group WU, DEFAULT: N_B); it checks the characterization build's warm-up definition where that differs.
- The same rule reaches CLONE_NON_REPLACE_CONTROL (BA04V5-02). Add characterization-build twins of the PW-CLONE variants, at least BASE and NESTED (the families that governing characterization-build runs import) and preferably all five for uniformity, or obtain the named transfer ruling with evidence that AR4-06 (3) requires.
- SIGNED_ZERO_CONTROL (Q-SIGNED-ZERO-CB) and SOURCE_SWAP_CONTROL (the negative control of Q-I13 and Q-I13-CB) already hold on each build.
- Update BA-02b: the WUM, S5CLO and CLONE rows; the Q, WU, PR-REC and PW-CLONE group rows; the enumerated sets of P1, P4 and P7 if they are made per build; and the counts of section 5 and the memo.
rulings.reasoning:
- V2.1 4.3: 'Every instrument I-01..I-16 must be qualified on the exact execution build before any governing run', and a governing run with an unqualified instrument cannot yield a PASS.
- V2.1 4.3.1: 'These controls are added to the qualification of section 4.3'.
- V2.2 PA-12, 'Qualification controls (amends V2.1 section 4.3.1)', adds CLOSURE_COMPLETENESS_CONTROL (I-13 with I-12) and WARMUP_BOUNDARY_CONTROL, and replaces CLONE_NON_REPLACE_CONTROL (SL-5 importer with I-13 and I-12).
- V2.1 2.1 makes 'instrument qualification records for the exact build' BUILD_BOUND, and AR4-06 (2) puts them in CHARACTERIZATION_TUPLE.
- These qualifications are consumed on the characterization build: 26 governing characterization-build scenarios exercise S5CLO, 30 exercise WUM and 5 exercise CLONE.
- AR4-06 (3) names Q-* and E6-C*, but it forbids transfer without evidence and a ruling. A restrictive reading would leave the closure, warm-up-boundary and non-replacing-import qualifications of the characterization build missing, and every run above could not yield PASS.

rulings.item: AR4-12 EXACT DELTA CHECK: does STATIC_REVIEWED (approved with the dynamic-trace plan on BA-06 V4 blob 5758f3c4) carry over to BA-06 V5 (blob e69a141d, LF SHA-256 6f7eaf5b...e934)?
rulings.reasoning:
My independent diff of blob 5758f3c4 against the V5 file shows the following.
- Design-time inventory (3 to 3.2.5: U-rows, C-rows, X-rows; 3.3: class table) and dynamic-trace plan (section 7; 10.2 columns; section 11 Ops(plan)): no content change. The only edits are 20 label substitutions (sibling version labels, and one 'BA-11 V4 section' -> 'BA-11 registry section' under AR4-17), the pointer 'is open question AQ-V4-14.' -> 'is ruled by AR4-15 (section 217; section 5).' in limit (3), and the insertion of limit (4). Limit (4) is exactly what AR4-12 (1) requires.
- The pointer substitution is content-neutral: AR4-15 rules 'ningún cambio de expectativa' and changes nothing in the trace.
- The two inventory components outside the spans (section 3 'Composition') changed only by ruling-mandated restatements. In section 5, AR4-07 adds HDM-CHAR-FXANNBLANK to the host-defaults row, and AR4-15 says 'BA-06 precisa su residuo de §5'. In section 12, the INVENTORY_REVIEW_RECORDS timing is the fix of the minors that AR4-12 (2) itself sends forward. The 17 residual rows, their 'affects' cells and the EVM field set/order are unchanged, so no operation class is affected and AR4-12 (2) has no class to re-review.
- V2.4 reopens review only when an operation is added. V24-N2 requires a new BA-06 version, not a new compilation, for design-inventory changes. AR3-22 set the exact-delta method.
- The checks script reproduces byte-identically, and all 28 bound hashes match.

rulings.item: AQ-V5-07: scope of the BA-06 frozen parts for the AR4-12 exact delta check (section 5 and 12 rows; the AQ-V4-14 -> AR4-15 label substitution)
rulings.reasoning: AR4-12 (2) ties re-review to 'la clase afectada', so the test is operation- and class-level. V2.4 reopens a class review when an operation is added. V24-N2 treats changes of the design inventory as needing a new BA-06 version. V2.2 PA-11 condition 7 (residuals) and condition 6 (differences resolved explicitly) define what the residual table and the review records are. AR3-22 established the exact-delta method with no new compilation. Treating a ruling-id pointer or a ruling-ordered restatement as a content change would force a re-review with no class to review. Letting review-record edits pass undeclared would let an inventory change hide in a disposition, hence the declared-edit and pointer-invariance condition.

rulings.item: AQ-V5-03: the BA-06 inventory corrections withheld under AR4-12 (C-72; DC-18 + row X-05; U-03/U-09 partition): record by ruling, or in a later version with re-review of the affected classes?
rulings.recommendation:
Do both, in sequence: the Architect fixes the content by ruling now, and the next (candidate) BA-06 version carries it under AR4-12 (2). A ruling alone is not enough.
- C-72: apply a marked amendment on the C-98 model ('captured once by the orchestrator in PREPARE-R at PR, inside the command after PL'; V2.1 5 row PR, 6; ALT-21D V4 3.1; AMB-09), extend the BA06-C5 exemption to C-72, and reword DC-41 to match. Class unchanged (OC-PREP-READ), so no re-review.
- DC-18: correct the disposition. The top-level reference is a sealed-list element read and compared in pass 1 and pass 2 against the ORACLE_SPEC value (V2.1 10.1, 10.2). This is a review-record edit and needs no re-review.
- X-05: add the supplementary row for SL-6 pass-1 and pass-2 reads of every sealed-list element and container enumeration (V2.1 10.1 to 10.3; OC-VERIFY-READ; expected write events none). This adds a row, so OC-VERIFY-READ gets a class-limited Architect re-review in that version's exact delta check (no new compilation, AR3-22 pattern).
- U-09 (AutoCadLibraryBlockQuery post-import presence query) moves to OC-PREP-READ, as the orchestrator's re-query (C-91; V2.1 6, 7; CQ-01 adopted).
- U-03 (BlockLibraryImporter.cs:67-80 at 3375aadb, the importer's own pre-clone Has(name) read of the document) should stay in OC-IMPORT as an SL-5-internal phase-0 read, unless the seam design removes it (V2.1 11.3 computes the ADD set in PREPARE-R; EXEC-3). Make OC-PREP-READ exclusive ('the orchestrator's AUTH-12 presence queries, not the importer's own reads').
- Re-review OC-IMPORT and OC-PREP-READ, class-limited. Every other class keeps STATIC_REVIEWED.
rulings.reasoning:
A sealed BA-06 must be self-consistent. PA-11 says 'the review record is a baseline artifact', and V24-N2 says changes of the design inventory require a new BA-06 version. A ruling-only record would leave sealed bytes whose DC-18 disposition contradicts V2.1 10.1 and 10.2, and whose classes overlap. AR4-12 (2) already routes BA-06 minors to a candidate version and sets the consequence of a content change: re-review of the affected class. AR4-20 applies all confirmed minors, and AR4-12 decides how for BA-06.
The split between content-neutral and content changes follows AQ-V5-07.
For U-03, the finding's mechanical fix (move it to OC-PREP-READ) is not right on the code: U-03 is inside the importer, while U-09 is the post-import AUTH-12 query. That is why this item needs a class re-review, not a byte edit alone.

rulings.item: BA-05 V5 section 7 'Choices of this version' (1) to (4), submitted for the Architect's exact delta check
rulings.recommendation:
ACCEPT all four.
(1) REJECTED precedence over UNKNOWN, provided the run-time mapping of finding BA05V5-01 is added.
(2) A missing DIMSTYLE variable gives UNKNOWN (omitted by the producer), while an extra variable or wrong kind gives REJECTED.
(3) A manifest memberKey must be a CLOSURE member key.
(4) linetypeScale, widthFactor, bulge, xScale, lineSpacingFactor, shapeScale and DIMSCALE are compared by EXACT_DOUBLE, and reference scale factors use TOL_SCALE.
rulings.reasoning:
(1) Either result denies a digest, and precedence makes conformance deterministic (RJ-25). Only the run-time mapping to UNKNOWN (V2.1 28.3, 21.6) is missing.
(2) This is fail-closed (V2.1 28.3: not computable => UNKNOWN) and answers R2:BA05V4-N02's concern: an I-12 that omits an unreadable variable now gets UNKNOWN, never a narrower digest.
(3) V2.1 11.3 derives the ADD set from the closure and defines REUSED_BOUND for nested and dependency closure members. V2.1 7 keys the manifest to them.
(4) The R1:BA05V4-08 required fix offered 'field-to-EXACT' routing or an exact default inside BA-05. No slot is added, and BA-08 V5 section 10 lists exactly the eight slots BA-05 names (AR2-35, AR3-17). The Selective product writes Dimscale = 1.0 and copies the ST-13 set, so exact comparison adds no false O4, and DIMSCALE no longer waits on TOL_SCALE (K-3).

findings.location: section 7: 'When IN_USE is appended' (line 343), U1 last sentence (line 345), U3 PIN_USE_AFTER_CLOSURE (line 347), the paragraph 'A run whose manifest or consumed pin is superseded or revoked before its IN_USE entry can be appended ... the run is INVALID (V2.1 29.1)' (line 350), and line 337 ('a superseded pin later found defective is revoked ... which marks the runs that consumed it')
findings.claim: IN_USE is now appended after the run ends, and use legality is checked against u. Together these make the status of a completed run depend on the order of two custody appends made after it: the run's IN_USE entry and a SUPERSEDED or REVOKED entry of its manifest or of a pin it consumed. If IN_USE comes first, the run is a recorded use that the closure merely 'marks'. If the closure comes first, the run cannot be recorded and V5 declares it INVALID. V2.1 21.1 lists no such INVALID cause. V2.1 29.1 is about a hash mismatch at the run, not a later closure. The same applies to a run in flight across a baseline-version change: it can never be recorded, and its status is not stated.
findings.required_fix:
Make run legality independent of post-run append order.
(a) Test the closure conditions of U3 and the manifest transition against the run's start, not against u. A SUPERSEDED or REVOKED entry recorded before the run-start anchor's ANCHOR_RECORDED entry makes the use illegal. A closure appended later does not block the run's IN_USE: the run is recorded and marked by the closure, like a run recorded before it. The manifest machine admits that IN_USE, since it is not a 'return to IN_USE'.
(b) Alternatively, require that no closure of a manifest or pin is appended while a started run that uses it has no IN_USE entry: the control plane appends pending IN_USE entries first. Declare this, since step 5 cannot check it.
In both cases, remove the V2.1 29.1 derivation of INVALID. State that a run's status follows V2.1 21.1/21.3 and 21.1.1 (a closure cause is adjudicated by a Coordinator ruling recorded in the attempt log). State the status of a run in flight across a version change. Update the model and cases if (a) is taken.

findings.location: 5.1 rule 3 ('A pin is consumed once an IN_USE entry lists it', line 178); section 7 U3 ('Every governing run records its pins this way', line 347); 5.1 pin-record fields (lines 149-160); cross-reference BA-04 V5 md section 2.1 ('each governing run lists', line 126) and BA-08 V5 HDM-3 (HDM-CHAR-* carry PIN_SLOTS FIXTURE_INSTANCE and LOCK_MODE)
findings.claim: BA-07 does not say whether non-governing runs that use the manifest and consume pins append IN_USE and list their pins. Examples: HDM-CHAR-* consume LOCK_MODE and FIXTURE_INSTANCE; E4-LEARN-R1-*, LK-* and WU-DRY-* consume FIXTURE_INSTANCE. BA-07 also records no link between a pin and the pins its source runs consumed. So a pin consumed only by derivation runs can be superseded within the version (rule 3 applies only to listed consumption). A downstream pin derived under the old one, such as HOST_DEFAULT_MAP derived by HDM-CHAR runs under the old LOCK_MODE, stays live. A governing run can then consume the new LOCK_MODE together with a map derived under the superseded mode, and verification is clean. This contradicts the ordering that AR3-11 condition 1 and AR4-07 impose (HDM-CHAR after the LOCK_MODE selection). The same pattern holds for pins derived on a fixture instance that is later replaced.
findings.evidence: Simulation S2 (generator verify()): mandatory prefix; PIN_RECORDED HOST_DEFAULT_MAP (sourceEvidence = HDM runs under LOCK_MODE p1); PIN_RECORDED LOCK_MODE' with supersedes = p1, followed by SUPERSEDED p1 (legal: p1 was never listed by an IN_USE); anchor; IN_USE consuming [LOCK_MODE', E04, HOST_DEFAULT_MAP] → PASS_WITH_DECLARED_LIMITS. V2.1 29.3: 'IN_USE: recorded at each use'. The AR3-01 mode keeps every other control, E-10 included, fail-closed, so these runs use the manifest.
findings.required_fix:
State that every run that uses a manifest, governing or not, appends IN_USE listing every pin it consumes. Keep rule 3's 'consumed' at governing consumption if the Architect prefers AR2-17's 'before the first governing run'.
Add the derivation link: a pin record lists the pin-record hashes its source runs consumed, for example `derivedUnderPins`. U3 then requires that every pin a run consumes was derived under pins that are still live and that the run itself consumes, where the run consumes that kind. A supersession or revocation of an upstream pin makes every pin derived under it unusable until it is re-derived.
Add a case to section 12 and to the model, or declare the model limit.

findings.location: 5.3 'Custody' (line 227) and 'Use' (line 229); section 7 U5 (line 349); section 10 last row (line 465)
findings.claim: The build-equivalence record is custodied as a review record, which has no later event. An equivalence found wrong after it was recorded therefore cannot be revoked in custody, and U5 has no condition that excludes it: the control plane keeps starting PRODUCT_BUILD runs that rely on it. U5 checks only that a record with matching build values is anchored before the run-start anchor. This is fail-open on the precondition under which AR4-06 (4) applies the characterization-build pins to product runs ('solo bajo esa equivalencia registrada'). A new record cannot correct it either, because the schema has no negative verdict.
findings.evidence: 5.3: 'an equivalence found wrong after it was recorded is a finding for the Coordinator, not a custody transition of this procedure (declared, section 10)'. U5: a record 'whose productBuild equals its own build values and whose characterizationBuild equals those of CHARACTERIZATION_TUPLE', whose 'REVIEW_RECORD_ADDED entry has an index at most the h of the run-start anchor'. 7 REVIEW_RECORD machine: 'no later event'. 5.3 'method' values: BYTE_IDENTICAL_PRODUCT_ASSEMBLIES and REVIEWED_DIFF only.

Either admit REVOKED (with cause) for REVIEW_RECORD subjects whose record kind is CT21D_BUILD_EQUIVALENCE, add to U5 'no REVOKED entry of that record at an index lower than the run-start anchor's ANCHOR_RECORDED entry', and update the model and a case. Update section 10.

rulings.item: AQ-V5-04 (a): the custody-log reference of the tuple field 'manifest hash and custody-log reference' as a per-manifest constant (the first anchor whose h covers the manifest's APPROVED entry), with the run-binding anchor carried separately as IN_USE.runStartAnchor
rulings.recommendation: ACCEPT, with the fixes of BA07V5-01 and BA07V5-05. Also state that the reference is computed from the anchors discovered at the remote (6.2 step 3), and that it stays unchanged when the manifest is carried over (consistent with AR4-13).
rulings.reasoning:
- V2.1 2 and 2.2: a BUILD_BOUND field must be equal in every governing run of an instance and must match the baseline profile. A 'latest anchor at sampling' value changes from run to run, so it would make every later run a tuple mismatch (INVALID); the R2 required fix was unworkable on this point.
- V2.1 2.1 records the field 'from the custody log', and V2.1 29.1 speaks of an 'immutable association with the tuple'.
- V2.1 29.3/29.4: the manifest's APPROVED -> ANCHORED transition, in model A (AR3-23), is the first ANCHOR_RECORDED whose h covers APPROVED. That anchor is naturally the manifest's custody-log reference.
- A per-run binding is session data, so V5 is right to keep it in the IN_USE entry (SESSION_BOUND-like), not in the tuple.

rulings.item: AQ-V5-04 (b): no supersession of a consumed LOCK_MODE, HOST_DEFAULT_MAP or FIXTURE_INSTANCE pin within one baseline version (5.1 rule 3, CONSUMED_PIN_SUPERSEDED); E04_ADMITTED_SET never; EVM_FROZEN allowed as a new model version
rulings.recommendation: ACCEPT, on two conditions. (1) Section 10 and the Owner Act 2 disclosures state the operational consequence: a consumed non-EVM pin found defective can be revoked, but its slot then stays empty until a new baseline version, and the slot's scenarios cannot run meanwhile. (2) The notion of 'consumed' is completed as in BA07V5-03, so that a pin used to derive another pin cannot be silently replaced.
rulings.reasoning:
- V2.1 21.3: 'Changing the scenario, the contract or the model is a new version, not a retry'; no cherry-picking; every governing attempt counts.
- AR2-11: E04 is 'no se revisa por retrospectiva'.
- AR2-17 and AR3-26: FIXTURE_INSTANCE and HOST_DEFAULT_MAP are 'fijado antes de la primera corrida gobernante'.
- V2.1 3.4: LOCK_MODE is selected by review before governing use.
- V2.1 1.7 and 2.1: pin-bearing values are BUILD_BOUND inputs, and a change creates a new instance with no transfer.
- The EVM_FROZEN exception is exactly V2.1 27.5 (new model version, review, revalidation; runs under the older version are not evidence for the newer). This is what R1:BA07-V4-01 required.
- AR4-13 leaves the within-version case open. The reading is the fail-closed one and adds no event.
- My C5 and C6 simulations behave as the rule states.

rulings.item: AQ-V5-04 (c): the carry-over block before the first anchor of v<k+1>, with mandatory REVOKED (SUPERSEDED_BY_RULING) of every live v<k> pin that is not carried over
rulings.recommendation: ACCEPT as the Architect's reading of AR4-13. No change of bytes is required.
rulings.reasoning:
- AR4-13 places 'esas entradas' before the first anchor of v<k+1> and makes the pin carry-over happen 'todo antes del primer uso gobernante'. Since U1 requires a run-start anchor of v<k+1>, 'before the first anchor' implies 'before the first governing use'.
- AR4-13 also rules 'a lo sumo un pin vivo por ranura'. Read per slot across versions, a non-carried v<k> pin must be closed before any v<k+1> pin of that slot can be recorded; otherwise PIN_SLOT_CONFLICT or CARRY_OVER_INVALID would be unavoidable. The mandatory REVOKED is therefore the mechanical consequence, not a new rule.
- V2.1 29.3: 'any state -> REVOKED (with a recorded cause)'. The cause SUPERSEDED_BY_RULING mirrors what AR4-13 names for a manifest that is not carried over, and it makes CARRY_OVER_MISSING checkable.
- The R2 pass recommended the same.
- My C1-C4 and C7-C9 simulations show the block closes the window that R1:BA07-V4-02 and R2:BA07-V4-02 found, with no new event type.

rulings.item: AQ-V5-05: the BA-08 V5 HDM-5 agreement rule (several runs that supply one HOST_DEFAULT_MAP entry must agree; otherwise UNKNOWN (O5); no choice between runs)
rulings.recommendation: ACCEPT as the Architect's reading of AR3-11 condition 4 and V2.2 PA-9, with two precisions. (1) The pin record keeps a disagreeing entry as present-and-UNKNOWN, citing the runs, rather than dropping it, so the lookup result is determinate. (2) HDM-7 states that the rule partly detects a dependence outside the key set across fixtures: HDM-CHAR-FX1F, FXANN and FXANNBLANK all supply entries for piece references and DBText at the same key tuple, so such a dependence becomes UNKNOWN instead of staying hidden. BA-10's fail-closed clause for S-1..S-3 then stands as written.
rulings.reasoning:
- AR3-11 condition 4: an attribute without an established value is UNKNOWN (O5).
- V2.2 PA-9 and AR2-16: the value is never derived from governing outputs, and no authority chooses between observations.
- V2.1 21.3: no cherry-picking among runs.
- V2.1 3.4 applies the same principle to LOCK_MODE: UNKNOWN 'when ... results differ across runs'.
- The R2 pass recommended exactly this addition for AQ-V4-07. AR4-07 and AR4-14 neither contradict nor state it.
- The rule is fail-closed: a disagreement costs a false rejection, which PARAM-03 counts, never an unsupported EQUAL.
- It changes no count (memo block E).

rulings.item: AQ-V5-06 (1): CHAR_RUNS(s) = N_det + 1 for the non-governing composition check EV-L-COMPOSED
rulings.recommendation: ACCEPT as a derived count on the Q-O3 pair, with no new Owner question. Q-O3 already discloses it. BA-10 should add the fail-closed basis: a missed unexplained or non-deterministic composed event is caught by the governing EV-V validation against f(plan) of the frozen EVM.
rulings.reasoning:
- V2.1 21.7: determinism repetitions are MUST_FIX with an explicit intent; BA-10 gives the PARAM-02 intent.
- AR4-01: EV-L-COMPOSED checks against a DRAFT or UNDER_REVIEW model, so there is no frozen f(plan). By the reference-by-use principle of AR3-24 (the first run is the reference for learning), the composed plan's only stable reference is its own first run. N_det + 1 gives N_det determinism trials and N_det + 1 trials against the composed model entries.
- V2.1 27.2 step 4: unexplained events block the freeze.
- A miss is fail-closed: the governing validation (V2.1 27.1, 27.2 step 6; E12-V, class B) compares every run with f(plan) of the frozen EVM (V2.1 27.4).
- Deriving counts from the Owner's pairs without a new question follows AR4-14 (b)(i).
- Cost: 30 runs at row1 (memo).

rulings.item: AQ-V5-06 (2): scope of the AR4-14 (b)(i) fail-closed statement (P-L5, P-L6, P-L7 not re-observed by governing runs; P-L4 unstated)
rulings.recommendation: ACCEPT the derived N_c with the scoped statement and the Q-O1 disclosure, with one change. BA-10 should state that P-L4 is re-observed and fail-closed: every governing mirror run executes PREPARE-R, PREPARE-W and MUTATION under the pinned mode, so a lock violation there aborts or refuses the run (typed seam failure, or a crash ruled under V2.1 21.1) and never stands behind a PASS. Wording to use: 'fail-closed for E-04 membership, P-L1..P-L4 and the S-1..S-3 lookups; P-L5..P-L7 rest on the V2.1 3.4 selection review'. No other count or ruling is needed.
rulings.reasoning:
- AR4-14 (b)(i) accepted the derived count because a missed behaviour fails closed at the consuming control. That premise is true for every behaviour a governing run re-observes: E-04 (V2.1 3.3), E-03's PL and continuity reads (P-L1..P-L3; V2.1 5), and, as shown above, P-L4.
- For P-L5..P-L7, V2.1 3.4 itself places the safeguard in the selection review: 'UNKNOWN when any property is unmeasurable or results differ across runs'; P-L7 is by definition a comparison across candidate modes. The contract does not require a governing re-observation of them.
- The LK-* runs carry the class-A detection intent of the Owner's pair (V2.1 21.7), and Q-O1 discloses the limit.
- The honest scope in V5 is therefore a correct application of AR4-14 (b)(i). Restricting the intent further, or adding a count, would have no contract basis.

rulings.item: AQ-V5-02 (WU-BOUNDARY part): must WU-BOUNDARY, the scenario of WARMUP_BOUNDARY_CONTROL, also run on the CHARACTERIZATION_BUILD?
rulings.reasoning:
- V2.2 PA-12 adds WARMUP_BOUNDARY_CONTROL 'to the qualification of section 4.3' (V2.1 4.3.1: 'These controls are added to the qualification of section 4.3. Each is a scenario of the catalog').
- V2.1 4.3 requires qualification 'on the exact execution build before any governing run'. V2.1 2.1 makes 'instrument qualification records for the exact build' BUILD_BOUND. AR4-06 (2) puts 'registros de calificación de ese build' into CHARACTERIZATION_TUPLE.
- AR4-06 (3) rules per-build qualification and 'no se dicta transferencia'. Its enumeration Q-*/E6-C* names the catalog's ids for that principle, not a narrower one.
- The boundary depends on build-specific code: the characterization build has its own manifest build layer and WUM set, harness switch assemblies, and E-11M/E-12 handlers with RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED handling (BA-09 section 5; BA-08 K-10). Governing CB runs (NC-WU-FOREIGN, the WR cells, the Q-I14-* vehicles, EA2) cross that boundary.
- V2.2 PA-1.x row WU requires 'boundary control passes'.
- Without a twin, CB governing runs would rest on a product-build qualification, which is the transfer AR4-06 (3) excludes.

rulings.item: R-01 Product SHA to bind the baseline to
rulings.recommendation: Bind the CT-21D baseline code facts and fixture specifications to origin/main 95690c28dc6268e61dff32a0cbc33cc9fde3d47f (a named BASELINE_PRODUCT_SHA recorded in BA-11). Two exceptions: (1) BA-06 keeps its frozen §3.1 inventory bound to 3375aadb and adds a delta annex (IMP-05); (2) if option (a) of IMP-01 is chosen, FX-ANN-BLANK uses the declared construction build 69daf03a. Do not keep 3375aadb or 1304101d, and do not bind to 69daf03a.
rulings.reasoning: (1) The governing and characterization builds must contain the integrated seams (EXEC-3; K-10 'a build of the product at the exact source SHA'), so their source SHA will descend from 95690c28. A baseline bound to 3375aadb would describe fixture routes and UI behaviour that no build under test will have. (2) Fixtures are built 'by the exact build', so they must reflect I-55 (G9b, first-view freedom, batch) and I-60. (3) Rebinding is cheap: the Selective drawing core is byte-identical from 3375aadb to 95690c28 (drawer, envelope writer, importer and cache, builders, editor state, codec, availability, catalogs), so the change is mostly identities and line citations. (4) BA-03 resolves its code identities against origin/main by design and has already drifted. (5) 69daf03a would let a blank name be built today, but it is not an ancestor of the future execution SHA's naming behaviour. Binding does not require reconciling the branch.

rulings.item: R-06 Drift control after this rebind
rulings.recommendation: Adopt a CODE_FACT_DELTA_CHECK rule (a decision, not errata). Before any candidate or seal ratification, run the BA-03 runner and a new BA-08 code-identity runner against the bound SHA. Before the first governing run, compare the bound SHA with the exact source SHA of each build under test. Any drift in a cited file requires either a new artifact version or a recorded Architect ruling. A later main advance triggers this check, not an automatic rebind.
rulings.reasoning: main advanced twice during the round without any mechanical signal to BA-08 or BA-06. BA-03 alone detected it. The exact execution SHA is necessarily later than any design-time bound SHA.

rulings.item: R-07 What I-55 and I-60 state about RACKMIRROR / I-52

I-55: it consumes AUTH-15 in G15 ('sin envolver ni clonar'); it has an Owner decision that RACKPROYECTAR admits and keeps legacy unnamed racks (G16 C16-05); CR-09 requires 'una autoridad por responsabilidad con I-52' and forbids NewRackId and re-stamping in ID19; ADR-0042 names ADR-0036 as a consumer of the same Foundation; the shared-view-foundation docs added to main are I-55's historical R1 reconciliation ('NOT REGISTERED by I-52 · NOT EFFECTIVE'). The only open I-52 product obligation, outside CT-21D, comes from that R1 table's X-6 row: C-2 baselines are to be re-established by whichever of I-52/I-55 integrates second, which is now I-52 at its G6. No I-55 or I-60 document mentions CT-21D, FX-ANN-BLANK or the mirror name.

rulings.item: Is the V2.4 rule 'an operation added by the implemented seams after the design-time review reopens the review of its operation class' triggered?
rulings.recommendation: No. It becomes applicable at the seam implementation review (EXEC-3) and in the E2 trace, if seam or orchestrator code reuses any I-55/I-60 code. Candidates: the RACKPROYECTAR reference append or AUTH-15 via projection (OC-REF-TOP, OC-BTR-VIEW, OC-ENVELOPE); RackSiblingScan in PREPARE-R (OC-PREP-READ); CreatePreparedBlock (OC-BTR-* transaction site). A product-SHA rebind is a different mechanism: it changes the design-time inventory and so requires a new BA-06 version and baseline (V24-N2). It is not a class reopen by this rule.
rulings.reasoning: The rule's subject is operations 'added by the implemented seams'. No seam exists: branch 86e331b3 has zero src changes relative to its merge base with main, and EXEC-3 has not started. The main advance adds product operations on product entries, not seam operations.

Also none for OC-LOCK, OC-LIB-ACQ, OC-TM, OC-TM-READ, OC-TOP-CHECK, OC-VERIFY-READ or OC-ABV-READ, which are contract-derived from an unchanged contract. OC-PREP-READ needs re-review only if AQ-V5-03 moves U-03/U-09 into it. The product-part rows that belong to no class also need an independent blind recompile of the changed entries (PA-11 conditions 1, 5, 6), because this assessment is the reviewer's own classification: D-01, the U-37/U-38/U-39/U-40 caller lines, U-41, the D-13 sites, U-34..U-36 and the MAIN95-06 reads. rulings.item: Is any I-55/I-60 code on the path the RACKMIRROR seams would reuse to create Selective views?
rulings.recommendation: No, under the governing texts. The seams reuse primitives that are all byte-identical: LateralHeaderDrawer.CreateSystemBlock, RackBlockData.Write/Read, RackBlockFinder.ScanEnvelopes, and the importer internals or a new structured SL-5 importer (P-4). None of the new code qualifies as a seam: (a) CreatePreparedBlock and RackViewPlacement take the lock and commit their own transaction, so they cannot be seams (V2.1 15.3). (b) BlockPlacement stays interactive and document-bound, so SL-4 cannot use it (BA-09 V5 1d). (c) The RACKPROYECTAR write scope is orchestrator-shaped but uses AUTH-15, which is precedent only under AR2-38 and misses C-127, and its import lock is not the single X-01 lock. (d) SiblingRedraw* is edit path (D-11). (e) RackNewRackName is excluded: I-60 does not apply it to projection or duplication, and the mirror name '<base> - espejo' is never blank. The residual risk is voluntary reuse at implementation; handle it by the V2.4 reopen at EXEC-3 (second ruling).

findings.artifact: CT-21D contract V2.1 §2 / §4.3 / §23 and BA-11 V5
findings.claim: The tuple fixes no hash. Its BUILD_BOUND 'repo source SHA of the build' comes from the build receipt of the build under test. The baseline's bound SHA is a different thing: where the static facts came from. No tuple field or mismatch rule compares the two. The tuple's 'Selective kind-authority version and hash' is only the BA-08 document hash, so a build whose reused product path has drifted from the bound SHA still passes V2.1 §2.2. V2.4 §1 reopens a class only for operations the implemented seams add, not for drift of the reused path. Conversely, if the bound SHA were written into the tuple as the source SHA, every governing run would be INVALID under §2.2. The build under test must contain the integrated seams (EXEC-3) and instruments (EXEC-2), which 95690c28 lacks.
findings.evidence: V2.1 L214: a run governs only if every BUILD_BOUND field equals the baseline. L220: 'repo source SHA of the build | BUILD_BOUND | build receipt'. L248: any BUILD_BOUND mismatch is INVALID. BA-11 V5 L149-155: library, CATALOG_FOLDER and manifest are 'fixed per build under test at execution preparation'. PA-11(1): the static enumeration is 'bound to the exact source SHA'. V2.4 §1: 'the reused product path at a bound SHA'.
findings.required_fix: The Architect rules one of two ways. As a reading, following AR4-06: an execution-preparation precondition for each build under test. Every (path, blob) pair of the reused product path cited by BA-03/BA-06/BA-08 at the bound SHA must equal the pair at the build's source SHA, or the delta is recorded and processed (class reopened; a design-time inventory change means a new BA-06 version and a new baseline). The result is kept with the tuple under BA-07 custody. Or as a pre-approved micro-errata V2.6 before the BA-01 candidate, which AR4-06 already allowed for a new tuple field. Either way, record expressly that the bound SHA is never a tuple value.

rulings.item: Q1 — Does anything on main now constrain I-52 / RACKMIRROR or CT-21D?
rulings.recommendation: No Freeze, ADR, ROADMAP entry or HANDOFF statement on main claims RACKMIRROR or CT-21D, and no clause of V2.1..V2.5 is contradicted. For the contract text this is NON-MATERIAL. For the code facts of BA-03/BA-06/BA-08/BA-09 it is MATERIAL (IA-G-02). Obligations that do bind now: IA-G-05 (V17 §8.5 C-2 re-establishment and the ADR-0042 re-read), IA-G-07 (G-M24 regeneration and T-GRD-08 classification) and IA-G-06 (FX-ANN-BLANK constructibility; Owner watch on mirror naming). These come from I-52's own Freeze or from main's product behaviour, not from a competing claim.
rulings.reasoning: Main keeps the division of authority. ADR-0042 L15-18 calls itself 'un ADR de producto' for I-55, and L239 names ADR-0036 only as a consumer of the same foundation. HANDOFF (main) L1948-1950: 'I-52 conserva reflection, mirror read-set y policy de RACKMIRROR; I-55 conserva … placement policy'. ROADMAP (main) I-55 row: 'compatibilidad con I-49 e I-52 sin depender de ellas'; I-57/I-58/I-59 rows: 'I-52 conserva policy … AUTH-15 permanece separado'. The I-60 Freeze scopes naming to its listed 'rack nuevo' routes, and RACKMIRROR is not among them. On the product side, RACKPROYECTAR's caller-owned write scope (RackProjectionWriteScope.cs L54-67 at 95690c28) creates only HeaderRun and Cantilever definitions; Selective frontal and planta have no caller-owned creation path, so F-2 and SL-1/SL-2/SL-4 face no competing authority. What does change is the Selective creation path that the baseline cites: RackSelectivoCommands, SystemBlockWriter, BlockPlacement, RackSelectiveWindow, ADR-0042 decisions 2-3, and I-60 auto-naming.

rulings.item: Q2 — What WORKFLOW requires for a branch behind main before its implementation gates, and who authorizes
rulings.recommendation: I-52 must rebase onto current origin/main. It must not merge main into the branch. The rebase is required by V1 §4.2 at every session opening and again at §4.5.1, and Owner validation or host evidence counts only on the rebased SHA (§4.5.3, §6). The rule needs no authorization. Only a deviation from it does, and that needs the Owner (WORKFLOW §10). The Coordinator schedules and scopes the reconciliation gate, as in the §104 precedent. See the required fix of IA-G-01 for the concrete steps.
rulings.reasoning: integration/I-56 classifies I-52 as T1, so V1 is definitive by Claim-Id. WORKFLOW §11.3 (L467-469) says a V1 unit reads current main except for clauses the normative merge modified, and 8a021fb6 did not touch §4. AGENTS.md (main) 'Reutilización de evidencia' says: 'Un rebase crea SHAs nuevos: la evidencia previa al rebase no valida el SHA rebasado'. WORKFLOW §11.5 route R is a V2 integration rule and does not govern I-52. The reconciliation is mechanically light: the branch has no src/tests/assets changes, and the merge-tree preview shows one ROADMAP conflict. Its governance cost is real, though: 136 SHAs are rewritten, which is why the archive tag and blob-identity carry-over are needed.

rulings.item: Q3 — Is binding the CT-21D baseline to 95690c28 (read-only, no merge) consistent with V2.1 §2 and the 'exact build' of V2.1 §4.3, given the build under test is built from the RACKMIRROR branch?
rulings.recommendation: It is consistent only as the bound SHA, i.e. where the static code facts come from (V2.4 §1 'a bound SHA'; PA-11(1); AR2-46 precedent 'SHA ligado e histórico'). It is never a tuple value. It is also consistent only if coupled with the IA-G-01 rebase onto 95690c28, or a later main with identical cited blobs, before any build under test exists, and with the IA-G-03 precondition checked per build. Without the rebase, re-binding creates a divergence that does not exist today (IA-G-02). 95690c28 is still the better forward choice than 3375aadb: any build satisfying EXEC-3 (IA-G-10) and WORKFLOW §4.5.1 will contain current main, so the 3375aadb facts are bound to drift.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 §2 fixes no concrete hash. Its BUILD_BOUND source SHA is sampled from the build receipt of the build under test (L220), and a mismatch makes the run INVALID (L248). The exact build of §4.3 (L421), EXEC-5 and EXEC-9 is that build, qualified per build (AR4-06). 95690c28 has neither seams nor instruments, so it can never be the exact build, and no evidence moves between builds (V2.1 §1.7; AGENTS exact-SHA; V18 §13 'El propio cambio de SHA no transfiere evidencia'). Also note: the rebase before integration (WORKFLOW §4.5.1) creates a new build, and therefore a new ALT21D_HOST_PASS instance, and CT-21D results do not transfer to it (§1.7). Which instance supports Owner Act 2 must be planned explicitly (ruling 'CT-21D instance').

rulings.item: Q4 — Which decisions belong to the Coordinator, the Architect and the Owner
rulings.recommendation:
COORDINATOR:
- the bound SHA (asked in §219.4)
- extending read-only extraction to 95690c28 (§212 authorized only 3375aadb and 1304101d)
- opening and scoping the reconciliation gate, including the archive tag, blob carry-over and CI
- sequencing baseline rounds before or after the rebase
- the reading of EXEC-3 (IA-G-10)
- hot-file serialization among active initiatives (WORKFLOW §7; HANDOFF main L1970 precedent: 'El Coordinador serializó I-53S primero')
- text verification of any errata
ARCHITECT:
- the technical impact rulings (which artifacts re-prepare; STATIC_REVIEWED carry-over by AR4-12(2))
- IA-G-03 as a reading or as pre-approved errata V2.6 text
- the FX-ANN-BLANK construction path (AR2-41)
- materiality of the ADR-0042/C-2 re-read against V18 §13, together with the Coordinator
OWNER:
- any exception to WORKFLOW V1 §4.2, §7 or §8 (deferring the rebase; intermediate HANDOFF edits)
- freezing main's Selective surface, or sequencing or blocking other initiatives' integrations until CT-21D executes
- whether RACKMIRROR falls under the I-60 naming rule
- Q-O1..Q-O5 (AR4-21)
- which CT-21D build instance supports Act 2
rulings.reasoning: The I-52 contract §0 sets the chain 'Owner → Coordinador I-52 ↔ Arquitecto I-52 → consenso → ejecutor', and the executor closes no product or architecture decision. WORKFLOW §10 (main) gives the Git and cadence domain to WORKFLOW.md, puts Owner decisions in decisions/<I>.md, and sends any other conflict to the Owner. LIFECYCLE §10 (main): 'Coordinator resuelve una errata o interpretación dentro de su dominio y Owner decide política'. Integration order across initiatives has been set by the Owner (decisions/I-60.md L14: 'do NOT integrate while I-55 awaits Owner Validation'), and only the Owner opens initiatives (WORKFLOW §2(d)). A freeze that constrains future initiatives is therefore Owner policy, not an I-52 gate decision. The contract precedent for the Architect is AR3-13 and §218: the Architect pre-approves errata text and the Coordinator verifies it.

rulings.item: Surface freeze of main's Selective code until CT-21D executes
rulings.recommendation: Do not propose an open-ended freeze. CT-21D execution is gated by EXEC-2..EXEC-12: the seams and instruments do not exist, host gates are pending, and Q-O1..Q-O5 are unanswered, so the freeze would last an unknown time. It would also block the Owner-listed follow-up on direct commands (HANDOFF main §4). Instead: (1) re-bind at a declared reconciliation point; (2) adopt the IA-G-03 per-build identity precondition, with detection by the BA-03 runner (fail-closed); (3) if anything, ask the Owner for a bounded coordination rule: an initiative that touches the cited Selective paths declares 'se estorba con I-52' and triggers an I-52 re-preparation notice.
rulings.reasoning: The cost of drift is bounded and already detectable: BA-03 exits 1 on identity drift, and BA-11 AR3-25 limits the cascade to unsealed dependents. A freeze trades that bounded cost for an unbounded roadmap constraint, and that trade is Owner policy.

rulings.item: Recommended sequence

1. Coordinator rules the bound SHA = 95690c28, conditional on reconciliation.
2. Reconciliation gate (IA-G-01): archive tag, rebase, blob-identity proof for all V2.x/BA files, ROADMAP conflict, push CI. Record the IA-G-05 and IA-G-07 obligations.
3. Architect delta review of V5 continues on the rebased tip, with agreements carried by blob as in §104.
4. Architect rules IA-G-03 (reading or errata V2.6) before the BA-01 candidate.
5. BA-03 V5 / BA-06 / BA-08 / BA-09 re-preparation at the bound SHA, then the rule-5 agreement and candidates (AR4-22).

votes.reasoning:
I checked every factual element at 86e331b3 (the worktree HEAD). All of them hold except one line citation.

**Facts that hold**
- **BA-03 V4 header.** Lines 17-19 read "before candidate: none beyond the authority identities of section 2 (bound by the specification; a drift re-prepares the candidate)".
- **BA-11 V5 row BA-03 (line 120).** It lists only V2.2 PA-14 items 3 and 4, both before seal. BA-11 V4 had the same omission, and neither R1 nor R2 flagged it.
- **Rerun output.** Its LF-normalized SHA-256 is e7db546a08b2b34b746b13aead9183461cc6e50e7de0f20625906b94b9723cb0, with identityDrift ["CMD"] and failed [].
- **RackSelectivoCommands.cs blob.** It is a22e6a6a at 3375aadb and at 1304101d, and f8e514a0 at 95690c28.
- **Runner.** It resolves "MAIN" sources at origin/main, so the drift stands whatever SHA the Coordinator binds, as PA-14 item 3 ("then-current identities") implies.
- **Section 5 BASE-12 (line 201).** It still says "BA-03 V4 ready in its bytes for candidate (AR4-19)". Decisions 219.4(a), in the same commit, says BA-03 V4 is no longer ready in substance.
- **BA-01 row.** It lists only V2.5 textual verification, the effective-contract agreement and the rule-5 agreement. By BA-11 section 2.1's own definition, a pending Coordinator decision that can change BA-01's content is a PREREQUISITE. Decisions 219.4 and HANDOFF both name the product-SHA decision as the next gate.
- **Diffs 1304101d..95690c28.** The stats match the claim: BlockPlacement.cs +/-132, RackSelectivoCommands.cs +/-114, SystemBlockWriter.cs +22 (CreatePreparedBlock), RackEditorSession.cs +61 (RackInsertionBatchContext, and RequestInsertViews also calls EnsureId). F-1 and F-3 of V2.1 15.1 may need errata, so the BA-01 gate matters.

**Citation error.** The claim cites BA-03 V4 line 143 for the exit-status-1 rule; that text is at line 131.

**Why the defect is real.** The registry is declared the only status authority. Its BA-03 and BA-01 rows and its BASE-12 line do not reflect the drift and the pending decisions that the same commit records. The BA-03 row is also not aligned with the BA-03 header's before-candidate clause, which is the alignment the AR4-17 / R1:BA11V4-02 fix required.

**Why I lower it to MINOR.**
1. Nothing can be wrongly sealed. BA-11 section 2 already makes the BA-03 CANDIDATE -> RATIFIED step fail closed. The seal-time re-run after a remote fetch re-prepares BA-03 on any drift or failure (AR4-19).
2. A candidate ruling is itself an Architect ruling on the exact bytes, and the drift is on record in decisions 219.4 and HANDOFF.
3. A later V2.6 would expire any premature BA-01 candidate through the cascade.
4. The fix touches only sections 3 and 5, outside the rule-5 sections, so it has no rule-5 effect.
5. "Ready in its bytes" quotes the AR4-19/217 ruling, and the bytes are in fact unchanged; only the substantive readiness is wrong.
6. Precedent: the analogous row/header gate inconsistencies (R1:BA11V4-02, R2:BA11V4-05) were rated MINOR.

The effect is a stale or incomplete status record, not a hole in the gates.

I checked the facts read-only at 86e331b3, 3375aadb, 1304101d and 95690c28. All of them hold, but only one part of the finding is a defect, and that part is minor.

**Facts verified**
- The output file I-52-ct21d-ba03-v4-rerun-at-main-95690c28-output.json hashes to e7db546a...23cb0. It records identityDrift ["CMD"], failed [] and originMain 95690c28.
- RackSelectivoCommands.cs is blob a22e6a6a at both 3375aadb and 1304101d, and f8e514a0 at 95690c28. RVA, SDL and COD are unchanged.
- The diff stats are as stated: SystemBlockWriter +22 (new CreatePreparedBlock), BlockPlacement 132, RackSelectivoCommands 114, RackEditorSession +61.
- The line citations are correct. BA-11 V5 line 120 matches V4 line 112 apart from the AR4-19 wording. Line 201 reads "BA-03 V4 ready in its bytes for candidate (AR4-19)".

**What is a real defect (MINOR)**
- Section 5 BASE-12 is stale. It contradicts decisions 219.4(a) in the same commit, which says "BA-03 V4 ya no está lista para candidato en sustancia (AR4-19: una deriva obliga a re-preparar)".
- The qualifier "in its bytes" (from the header of 217) no longer holds. BA-03's own identity rule means a drift requires re-preparation, which is a byte change.
- Fix (3), plus a note in the BA-03 row that the 95690c28 re-run failed (with the e7db546a output hash), is a legitimate in-place correction. Sections 3 and 5 lie outside the rule-5 sections, so it has no rule-5 effect.

**Why it is not MAJOR, and why the gate additions are not defects**
1. The claim that BA-11 section 2 gates DRAFT -> CANDIDATE_FOR_SEALING "only on the entry's PREREQUISITES" is wrong. The transition first requires "an Architect ruling on the exact bytes". Those bytes include BA-03's identity rule and its header text "a drift re-prepares the candidate". So the registry does not "admit" a drifted BA-03 candidate. Only an Architect ruling can, and the Architect is the one assessing the drift now.
2. The BA-03 PREREQUISITES cell is not a misalignment.
   - BA-11 section 2.1 defines PREREQUISITES as external inputs: host observations, decisions, rulings and construction work.
   - The BA-03 header says "before candidate: none beyond the authority identities of section 2 (bound by the specification ...)". That identity binding is part of the artifact's content, not an external input.
   - AR4-19 (section 217 prevails) places the fetch-and-compare of remote identities at the seal-time re-run and records it in the ratification. The V5 row applies AR4-19 verbatim.
   - The row is unchanged in substance from V4. R1:BA11V4-02 audited every row against its header and did not flag BA-03.
   - Adding a new before-candidate gate would harden the rule beyond AR4-19. It is not a correction the governing texts require.
3. The BA-01 gate is already handled by the governed sequence, and adding it now would pre-empt decisions not yet taken.
   - The BA-01 row already gates its candidate on "Coordinator textual verification of V2.5 and agreement of the effective contract".
   - Decisions 219.4 and HANDOFF, in the same commit, route the read-only impact assessment of 1304101d..95690c28 and the Coordinator's product-SHA decision ahead of any candidate ruling. The HANDOFF line reads "Siguiente gate: revisión delta del Arquitecto de V5 con evaluación de impacto ..., luego decisión del Coordinador sobre el SHA".
   - V2.1 15.1 is explicitly dated ("verified on main 3375aadb"). Whether errata is needed is exactly the assessment that is pending.
   - Under section 218, the Implementer was not authorized to create gates or decisions reserved to the Architect or Coordinator. Recording them is for the coming rulings, not a V5 defect.
   - "Exactly the code that 15.1 states" is also overstated. CreateBlock itself is untouched (a new CreatePreparedBlock is added), and F-3's EnsureId in the UI still holds. The PlaceBlockWithJig beforeCommit variant may bear on F-1, but that belongs to the impact assessment.

**Net result**

I checked the code and it confirms the claim. No V5 file handles the issue, so the item stands.

1. **What I-60 does on every new-rack path at 95690c28.** `RackNewRackName.Resolve` (src/RackCad.Plugin/Systems/Shared/RackNewRackName.cs) is called on each path. `RackLogicalNameAllocator.IsUnassigned` treats null, empty or blank as unassigned and returns "Selectivo N". The call sites are:

2. **The edit path cannot blank the name either.** RACKEDITAR runs `var name = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(window.RackName) ? embed.Name : window.RackName` (RSC:127 at 95690c28; the same at 1304101d:121). Clearing the name box keeps the existing name. AUTH-15 and RACKPROYECTAR only preserve an existing blank name on legacy racks; they never create one. RACKDUPLICAR and RACKLAYOUT already give non-empty names (I-60 freeze section 5).

3. **So no I-60 build can produce the fixture as specified.** BA-08 V5 sections 4.1, 12.1 and 12.6 say the instance is "drawn by the exact build through its editor" as a new rack with a blank Name. Section 4.1 still cites RSW and RSC at 3375aadb: an empty name box with no validation, and `system.Name = name`. On an I-60 build the frontal gets "Selectivo 1" and, with `DrawRackName` on, draws the label and creates `RACKCAD_ANOTACIONES`. The instance then fails its own conformance check (the layer must be absent).
   - Construction workarounds fail as well. Blanking the name later is impossible (point 2).
   - Only a drawing from a pre-I-60 build could hold such a rack. That departs from the "exact build" rule and would need a ruling.

4. **The execution build will contain I-60.** EXEC-3 (V2.1 section 23) requires the seams to be "implemented and integrated" in `src/`. In this repo "integrated" means merged into main, and main already contains I-60 (95690c28). Only a revert would avoid it.

Section 219.4 says the Implementer does not resolve it and asks the Architect for an impact assessment. No AR4 decision covers it, since section 219.4 is newer than section 217, so nothing in V5 counts as the required fix.

6. **Why BLOCKING is defensible.** Three things depend on FX-ANN-BLANK:
   - the sealed AR4-07 scenario `HDM-CHAR-FXANNBLANK`, one of the four required sources of the K-4 `HOST_DEFAULT_MAP` pin, which must be fixed before governing S-1..S-3 runs;

   A blank-named source is still valid in the product as a legacy state (I-60 freeze section 5), so the scenario still matters. Fixing it needs an Architect/Coordinator ruling on a new construction and the product SHA binding.

I checked this myself at 95690c28, and it holds.

(1) Every route that creates a new Selective rack now fills in a blank name.
- RackSelectivoCommands.cs:518-524 (DrawSelectiveView, the only new-rack entry used by RACKSELECTIVO/RS and the single-view menu) calls RackNewRackName.Resolve before serializing the document and the envelope.
- The menu batch path does the same at RackMenuCommands.cs:98-104.

(2) The edit path cannot clear a name. RackSelectivoCommands.cs:127 sets name = IsNullOrWhiteSpace(window.RackName) ? embed.Name : window.RackName. This line already existed at 1304101d:121. Clearing the box in RACKEDITAR therefore keeps the stored "Selectivo N". The I-60 freeze (section 4, section 5) confirms that edit, duplicate, layout and projection routes never assign a name and never blank one.

(3) The only blank-named Selective racks left in an I-60 build are legacy ones, which I-60 freeze section 5 keeps valid and never renames. BA-08 V5 section 12.6 (line 409) requires each fixture to be "drawn by the exact build through its editor". So FX-ANN-BLANK cannot be instantiated by any build that contains I-60. (5) The V5 files do not handle this at all: grep finds no mention of I-60, 95690c28 or RackNewRackName in any V5 artifact or in the delta3 evidence. No AR4 decision governs it; section 219.4 explicitly leaves it unresolved. It is not refuted.
